# Erdős Problem 71

*References:*

- [Bo77] Bollobás, Béla, *Cycles modulo $k$*. Bull. London Math. Soc. (1977), 97-98.

namespace Erdos71

/--
Is it true that for every infinite arithmetic progression $P$ which contains even numbers
there is some constant $c=c(P)$ such that every graph with average degree at least $c$
contains a cycle whose length is in $P$?

In [Er82e] Erdős credits this conjecture to himself and Burr. This has been proved by
Bollobás [Bo77]. The best dependence of the constant $c(P)$ is unknown.

The infinite arithmetic progression is encoded as a set $P \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ satisfying
`P.IsAPOfLength ⊤` (which forces a positive common difference), and "contains even numbers"
as the existence of an even element. The average degree of a finite simple graph is
`SimpleGraph.averageDegree`, i.e. $(\sum_v \deg v)/|V| \in \mathbb{Q}$, and a cycle whose
length is in $P$ is a cycle walk `w` with `w.length ∈ P`.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/Jayyhk/erdos-lean/blob/110d489ed5c07e5b216453e092e9113127c98c9a/problems/71/Erdos71.lean"]
theorem erdos_71 : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ P : Set ℕ, P.IsAPOfLength ⊤ → (∃ n ∈ P, Even n) →
      ∃ c : ℚ, ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V)
        [DecidableRel G.Adj], c ≤ G.averageDegree →
          ∃ (v : V) (w : G.Walk v v), w.IsCycle ∧ w.length ∈ P := by
  sorry

end Erdos71

reformulations.difference: An infinite arithmetic progression is represented by `P.IsAPOfLength ⊤`, without an explicit positive-common-difference hypothesis.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Proved in `/workspace/review/scratch.lean` that this is equivalent to `∃ a d : ℕ, 0 < d ∧ P = Set.range (fun n : ℕ => a + n * d)`. The cardinality condition excludes empty sets, singletons, and common difference zero; a positive difference makes the generating map injective and its range infinite.

reformulations.difference: The threshold is rational, and the graph quantifier includes empty finite vertex types.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Proved both relevant equivalences in `/workspace/review/thresholds.lean`. A real threshold can be increased to a rational threshold, and a rational threshold is also a real threshold. A threshold valid for nonempty graphs can be replaced by `max c 1`, which excludes empty graphs because their average degree is zero. Restricting an all-graphs statement to nonempty graphs gives the converse.

review.notes:
Checked the sole declaration against the official statement and accessible primary passages. No mathematical or status defects found: the source records an affirmative, Lean-verified solution, matching `answer(True)`, `research solved`, and the proof attribute.

Independent Lean checks verified the handshaking formula, average degrees for empty and small complete graphs, exclusion of cycles shorter than three, and a concrete triangle. They also proved that one even member of an infinite AP yields arbitrarily large even members, and that every rational degree threshold is met by some complete graph. Thus neither the zero boundary nor the degree hypothesis makes the statement vacuous.

The linked proof states exactly the theorem's right-hand side. It targets Lean 4.28; a sandbox copy compiled against the available Lean 4.33.1 after compatibility-only elaboration options and explicit height annotations. Its axiom audit returned only `propext`, `Classical.choice`, and `Quot.sound`.

Full texts of Bo77 and Er97b remained inaccessible behind publisher restrictions. Their bibliographic records were checked; the official statement and Er95 explicitly supply the claim needed for this review. No repository files were edited.
